rubric_items.reason: All eleven known REQs are traced: REQ-1..4 by S-1, REQ-5..7 by S-2, REQ-8..10 by S-3, REQ-11 by S-4. No assumed REQs.
REQ-11 moved to its own story S-4 (prior F-4 addressed). S-3 still groups the doctor link with the two data-exclusion constraints, but they are small and closely related.

ACs are Given/When/Then and discriminating: S-2 covers changed-after-booking and each Inactive partition, S-3 now checks the received data, S-4 covers every status. Cancelled partition checks fewer fields; fee grouping still untested.
The only values (50000 and 12345 paise) are converted to rupees inline using the glossary paise definition; (Inactive) marker comes from A-01.
Terms match the intent and glossary; body matches front matter; resolved findings and the open Q-02 are stated clearly.

findings.text: S-4 AC3 (Cancelled) checks only cancellation reason, actions and history, while the other status ACs also check time, doctor name, patient name and reason for visit. A change that breaks those fields only on Cancelled pages would pass.

cites.quote: then the cancellation reason, actions and history are the same as before this change
The appointment page today shows the appointment's time, doctor name, patient name, reason for visit, `cancellation reason` and history.

findings.suggested_fix: Extend S-4 AC3 so time, doctor name, patient name and reason for visit are also unchanged for a Cancelled appointment.

findings.text: Prior F-2 is still open and not listed under resolves: both fee ACs use fees under 1,000 rupees, so a page that formats the fee differently from the doctors list for larger amounts (e.g. thousands grouping) would still pass REQ-4.

cites.quote: then both show the fee as ₹123.45, with ₹ and two decimals
The fee is shown the same way as on the doctors list

findings.suggested_fix: Make S-1 AC4 use a fee of 1,000 rupees or more (for example 150000 paise, 1500 rupees) and compare it with the doctors list.

cites.quote: The fee is shown the same way as on the doctors list: `₹` with two decimals.
One hundredth of a rupee. Fees are stored and sent as integer paise.
Blood group, allergies, chronic conditions, current medications and notes of one patient.
A doctor, patient, department or specialization kept for history but not offered for new use.
